content:
alex: quick question — i'm drafting a compact routing policy payload for tiers + region fallback. goal: let console show minimal options but allow tenants to opt into variant lists. thoughts?

sam: curious what "compact" means here. flat list vs nested overrides?

alex: compact = single object per tenant with optional keys instead of huge nested tree. e.g.
```json
{
  "tenant_id": "t-acme",
  "tier": "pro",
  "region_prefs": [{ "region": "eu", "variants": ["redwood-small-q4", "redwood-medium-q3"] }],
  "fallback": ["pro-default", "free-default"]
}
```

Priya: love the compactness. telemetry-wise we need explicit labels for which decision branch was taken (exact tenant override vs tier default vs region fallback). otherwise ops can't surface regressions.

maria: +1 on telemetry. also gotta consider quota enforcement order. if quota reject happens, we should record that we tried fallback variant selection vs we short-circuited. ambiguous traces = pain.

sam: edge case: tenant override list could include variants that are incompatible with region (gpu vs cpu). policy should validate and either filter or include an explicit compatibility tag.

alex: agreed. i'm leaning toward pre-validation at policy upload time and runtime filter as safety net. console will warn on incompatible picks.

Priya: UI idea: single slider for "latency vs cost" per tenant that maps to an ordered variant list under the hood. keeps console simple but expressive.

maria: about quota enforcement: do we check plan quota first or routing availability first? scenario: pro tenant at quota limit but pro-default variant still available — should we fallback to cheaper variant or reject?

sam: we discussed two semantics earlier: conservative = enforce quota before routing (reject early), lenient = allow routing to cheaper variant if policy allows cross-tier fallback. we should make it explicit in policy: "quota_policy": "enforce"|"allow_fallback"

alex: good call. default to conservative but allow tenant opt-in to allow_fallback for burst savings. need audit log when allowed.

Priya: telemetry labels to add: decision_path (array), quota_checked (bool), quota_result (allowed|exceeded), fallback_triggered (bool), selected_variant. that makes golden signal dashboards easier.

maria: rollout UX: when ops flips a new variant ordering or grants allow_fallback, we should support canary rollouts at tenant subset level + gradual metric checks (latency, cost, quality regressions). deploy-bot can post canary status.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started for policy-update t-acme -> 5% tenants, monitor metrics: latency_p50, token_cost_avg, generation_quality_score.

sam: API shape debate: should console calls be thin and rely on server to expand compact entries, or should console send fully expanded policy? thin call preferred to keep validation central.

alex: thin call + server expansion + preflight validation endpoint. console will call /policy/preflight which returns warnings and compatibility fixes.

Priya: also add a telemetry tag for preflight_warning_count, so UX can show how many issues were surfaced.

maria: race condition note: two updates could overlap and cause inconsistent runtime cache. we need versioned policy objects and optimistic concurrency on write. if write fails, console shows diff and retry.

sam: agree — include policy_version and last_applied_version in telemetry.

alex: ok next steps: i'll prototype compact schema + preflight endpoint mock. Priya, can you sketch telemetry labels you need? Maria, can you write a short doc about quota enforcement semantics and concurrency safeguards? Sam, help with validation rules for variant compatibility.

Priya: will send a short list in #eng-telemetry today.

maria: i'll draft the quota semantics doc and share for review by EOD.

sam: i'll start a validator PR with a small compatibility matrix.

alex: thanks team. one more micro bike-shed: naming for the boolean that allows cross-tier fallback — "allow_cross_tier_fallback" vs "allow_fallback_on_quota". prefer the latter (more explicit).

maria: +1 for explicit.

Priya: tiny perf note: if we log full decision_path for every request it will be high cardinality. recommend sampling + aggregated counters. add "decision_sample_rate" per tenant.

alex: good call. default sample 1% and higher for tenants in canary.

deploy-bot: canary at 5% applied. policy_version v1.3 queued for rollout.

sam: leaving a final thought — make fallback semantics idempotent so retries don't pick different variants mid-retry. store request decision token during request lifetime.

maria: ok locking the plan: alex will prototype, deliverables: schema + preflight API + basic telemetry labels + concurrency strategy. follow-up sync tomorrow after PRs land. :thumbsup:
